turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Who decided on Owen's zero, and why did he find out on his phone in the middle of a class?
Okay isn't an answer. If you have nothing to show me, I'm going to the principal's office when I leave this room.
You asked for this meeting, Hale, and you've given me nothing. Withdraw the zero today, or I'm upstairs with my copy of your own procedure.
Okay to what, Hale? If the zero is coming off, say so, and I'll want it in an email tonight.
One letter isn't a commitment. I'm writing down that you have shown me nothing and said nothing. Say the words, Hale, or I walk upstairs.
Three times now, Hale, and still no answer. Full sentence: is the zero coming off Owen's mark, yes or no?
Sorry. The essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet.
Show me. Which line, on which page of Owen's essay, and where's your copy of the play? A student misquoting Shakespeare is a misquote, Hale, not a reason for a zero.
